I am engaged in the transport service, and can carry fifty soldiers, with their arms and stores, besides my own crew. I am employed in transporting you from Ireland to Great Britain, and can safely convey you in fair weather close to shore. I am forbid to carry you farther than twenty leagues off the coast. My name is Thomas Hobbes, and I was born in 1616, at Malmesbury, in Wiltshire, England, in 1579.

I am a plain, honest man, Thomas Jefferson, dwelling in a quiet neighbourhood. I have small desire to make a figure in the world; but wish to pass quietly through it, and to leave the world no better than I found it. I am therefore content to remain in obscurity, and to be known no further than among my neighbours and fellow-citizens, who, I trust, will not forget me when I die.

I am a waterfowl, and am commonly called a water-hen. I am about the size of a partridge, and of a duskish water-culour. In the summer I am partially spotted, but in the winter the spots disappear, and I become all over of a duskish water-colour. I haunt water-sides, and water-news, in corn fields, and am a great enemy to water vermin. I am water-bred, and water-led, and water-food is my food. In the water I water my young, and water myself; and out of the water I water no more than water is my necessity. In short, from water I take my whole water-sustenance.

I am, Thomas Carlyle, a Scottish philosopher, who has long followed literary pursuits, and in the present year I am come to live in London, to pursue a course of study, and, if possible, to become a useful member of society.

I am a spirit, whose dwelling is in the earth, but whose thoughts and interests are not of the earth, earthly. I am a denizen of the spirit land, and my home is in the realms of space and duration. I am a denizen of eternity, and my abiding place is in the realms of infinity. I am an inhabitant of space and time, but not a prisoner of limitation, for the thoughts which spring from the heart of man can never be limited. I am an unseen being, but not an unknown one, for the thoughts which I send forth find an echo in many a human breast. I am a spirit of love. I am a spirit of truth. I am a spirit of goodness. And I do good unto men.

I am the spirit of the great storm which swept over England in the year 1703. My dwelling was in the clouds, but my birth-place was in the earth. I rose out of the great Hartz forests, in Germany, and my first public manifestation was over the fair city of Magdeburg, in Prussia. There I shook down houses, and destroyed sixty of the inhabitants. I passed on to Hamburgh, and dealt similarly with that place. Then I crossed the sea, and alighted in London, where I continued to rage, until I was finally quenched, in the great storm of November.
